issues.item: Catastrophising Others: I worry obsessively about bad things happening to people I care about
issues.explanation: 'Catastrophising Others' is hard to integrate with the rest of the profile and the trauma type. The other items center on childhood physical abuse, mistrust, touch-sensitivity, fragmented memory, guilt, and self-damage; obsessive worry about harm befalling loved ones points to a different threat theme and is not supported by the appraisals or memory content.

issues.item: Door and Lock Checking: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
issues.explanation: 'Door and Lock Checking' suggests a home-intrusion/security threat theme. In this profile, threat is otherwise expressed as interpersonal danger cues (unexpected touch, ominous silence) linked to caregiver abuse. Without matching appraisals or memory content about break-ins or external intruders, this item is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the selected items.

vignette: As a child, Julian had grown accustomed to the sound of his mother's anger - the raised voice, the slamming doors, and the inevitable physical blows that followed. One particular incident stood out in his mind, though he couldn't quite piece together the events leading up to it. He remembered being in his room, hearing his mother storming down the hallway, and then feeling a searing pain on the side of his face. What happened next was a blur. Years later, as a successful fashion designer, Julian's life seemed put together - he had a thriving career, a network of friends, and a comfortable home in the city. However, beneath the surface, he struggled with an overwhelming sense of mistrust towards others. He couldn't shake off the feeling that people were waiting for him to slip up so they could pounce. This paranoia often led him to ruminate on past interactions, dwelling on what others had done to him and how he could have avoided those situations. He would also get caught up in self-blame, replaying moments where he felt he'd failed or made mistakes. Julian's inability to recall the traumatic event with clarity only added to his distress. When fragments of memories did surface, they were shrouded in guilt - he couldn't understand why he hadn't been able to protect himself or stop the abuse. These feelings of inadequacy reinforced his negative self-appraisal that he had permanently changed for the worse since the event. As a result, Julian's daily life became a minefield of potential threats. The slightest touch from someone could send him into a state of high alert, making him jump with alarm. He'd find himself on edge even in his own home, constantly scanning the surroundings for signs of danger. Unusual silences would also unnerve him - he'd feel an impending sense of doom, as if something terrible was about to unfold. These hypervigilant states would, in turn, trigger memories of the traumatic event, albeit fragmented and unclear. The more Julian tried to recall what had happened, the more his mind seemed to fog over, leaving him feeling numb and disconnected from his own experiences. This sense of disconnection only served to reinforce his negative self-appraisal that he was damaged beyond repair. The cycle of rumination, threat monitoring, and memory fragmentation continued to escalate, with each component feeding into the others. Julian's growing conviction that he was going crazy - that his reactions since the event were proof of his own instability - made him increasingly withdrawn. He stopped attending social gatherings, fearing that his anxiety would get the better of him. One day, while working on a new design project, Julian found himself paralyzed by fear - what if someone touched him unexpectedly? What if he lost control and had an episode in front of clients? The weight of these worries finally broke him, and he realized he needed help. As he sat in his darkened apartment, surrounded by the silence that now felt so oppressive, Julian knew it was time to confront the demons he'd been trying to outrun for decades. He hoped that therapy would provide a safe space to unravel the tangled web of memories, emotions, and negative appraisals that had come to define him. Most of all, he longed to break free from the suffocating grip of fear and mistrust, and learn to trust himself - and others - once more.
